title: Bluehead chub capture histories, Indian Creek, South Carolina: PIT-tagged fish, 15 bimonthly electrofishing occasions, November 2015 - March 2018
creator: Kanno, Yoichiro; Kim, Seoghyun; Pregler, Kasey (Colorado State University)
citation: Kanno, Y., Kim, S. & Pregler, K. (2022). Capture history data for: Sub-seasonal correlation between growth and survival in three sympatric aquatic ectotherms [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.np5hqbzxh
abstract: Cormack-Jolly-Seber capture histories of 429 PIT-tagged bluehead chub (Nocomis leptocephalus, >= 60 mm total length) in a 740 m reach of Indian Creek, South Carolina, sampled every two months by two-pass backpack electrofishing, November 2015 - March 2018 (15 occasions). One row per fish per occasion, y = captured; rows before first capture are 0. Sibling tables hold the other two species of the same survey.
samplingProtocol: Every two months (mean 61 days, range 48-70) the 740 m reach, divided into 20 m sections, was sampled upstream by two-pass backpack electrofishing (Smith Root LR-24, Halltech HT-2000), each occasion taking 1-10 days; fish at or above the tagging length were PIT-tagged (8 mm), measured and returned to their section (Dryad methods; Kanno et al. 2023).
surveyEvidenceNote: The deposited capture-history matrix has 15 occasion columns and every fish is surveyed at every occasion, including occasions before its first capture (y = 0).
closure: open between periods (bimonthly occasions; survival and emigration between occasions, CJS)
geographicCoverage: Indian Creek, Sumter National Forest, South Carolina, USA (a 740 m study reach); no coordinates deposited
notes: One of three tables from one deposit (ruling #20: one table per taxon of marked individuals); the others are kanno_2022_creek_chub_cjs and kanno_2022_mottled_sculpin_cjs. Periods are the bimonthly occasions (month and year in __periods; occasion dates and the 1-10 day sampling windows are not deposited). Rows before first capture are 0: drop them to condition on first capture. PIT tag numbers are not usable (the deposit stores them in scientific notation); units are the deposit's Obs_ID.

notShipped.PIT tag ids: PIT_Tag_ID is stored in scientific notation (4 distinct values for 2,021 fish); Obs_ID is the key
notShipped.lengths: total lengths at capture used for the paper's growth models are not in the deposit
notShipped.other species: in the sibling tables kanno_2022_creek_chub_cjs, kanno_2022_mottled_sculpin_cjs
